title: Kingdom of Thailand

endonym.native: ราชอาณาจักรไทย

capsule: The Kingdom of Thailand, known as Siam until 1939, became a constitutional monarchy on 24 June 1932 when the Khana Ratsadon (People's Party) ended the absolute rule of the Chakri dynasty in a bloodless coup, replacing Rama VII (Prajadhipok) with a constitutional framework. The country spent most of the twentieth century under military-dominated governments, with Plaek Phibunsongkhram aligning with Japan during World War II and Field Marshal Sarit Thanarat establishing an authoritarian development state in the 1950s–1960s; a brief democratic interlude (1973–1976) was followed by a rightist coup in October 1976. King Bhumibol Adulyadej (Rama IX, r. 1946–2016) provided institutional continuity across twelve constitutions and seventeen coups; his death in October 2016 preceded the accession of King Vajiralongkorn (Rama X) and a return to elected government following the 2019 elections.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Thailand's national boundaries are precisely defined by international treaties; the 1932 start date reflects the constitutional transition, not a territorial change, and modern borders are unambiguous.
